# Feature support for Vault Enterprise

@include 'alerts/enterprise-only.mdx'

Prior to 2026, HashiCorp offered Long-Term Support (LTS) for specific
Vault Enterprise releases. Starting with the April 2026 (2.x.x) release, Vault
Enterprise follows the IBM Support Cycle-2 (SC2) model.

The release cadence and fix policy described here apply to Vault Enterprise
and HCP Vault Dedicated 2.x and later. Vault 1.x releases retain their existing
maintenance terms. For HCP Vault Dedicated, version availability and upgrade
timing follow the service's [version management guidance](/vault/cloud/versions).

## Vault versioning

@include 'version-syntax.mdx'

### Release cadence

Vault plans four feature release windows each year: an annual major in May,
starting with 3.0 in May 2027, and minors in February, August, and November.
Patches target a monthly cadence for releases eligible for fixes. Release
windows are planning targets and may change. Refer to the
[release notes](/vault/docs/updates/release-notes) for available releases.

### Feature and fix availability

New features go into the latest minor of the current major. Features are not
backported to earlier minors or older majors.

Bug and security fixes go into the latest minor of each major that remains
eligible for fixes. For example, when 2.2 becomes available, upgrade from 2.1
to 2.2 and apply its latest patch to receive subsequent fixes.

The **final minor** is the last minor released within a major version. After
the next major ships, that final minor continues to receive eligible fixes
under its major's remaining support lifecycle.

When 3.0 ships, new features move to 3.x, while the final 2.x minor remains
the destination for eligible 2.x fixes. A final minor does not start a new
support period or receive a new LTS designation. Fix availability depends
on the major's support phase; Sustained Support does not include new fixes.

## What is Support Cycle-2 (SC2)?

The Support Cycle 2 uses a "2 + 1 + 3" framework to determine coverage for usage
support and product updates:

- **2** years of base support.
- **1** year of critical [extended support](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/7008589).
- **3** years of [sustained support](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/7008619),
  which **does not** include new fixes or enhancements.

The lifecycle starts with the major release. Minor and patch releases do not
restart it. Refer to [IBM Software Support Lifecycle](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/lifecycle/)
for official product dates.

The following table outlines the expected product updates and technical support
coverage for each support phase.

Product update                | Base support | Extended support | Sustained support
----------------------------- | ------------ | ---------------- | -----------------
New features                  | Yes          | No               | No
Non-critical bug fixes        | Yes          | No               | No
Product improvements          | Yes          | No               | No
Critical bug fixes            | Yes          | Yes              | No
Security patches              | Yes          | Limited          | No
Technical support case access | Yes          | Yes              | Yes

New features and product improvements follow the current major's latest minor.
Base Support for an older major does not include backports of new features.
Fix coverage depends on the support phase and applicable terms; technical
support case access does not guarantee a new fix for your installed minor.

For additional details on technical support coverage, please contact your account
representative or refer to the support article on
[IBM article on Support Cycle-2 (SC2) coverage](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/ibm-software-support-lifecycle-policies#Support_Cycle).

## Coverage for existing LTS versions

Existing long-term support versions follow the existing standard and extended
support periods. Standard maintenance for a given Vault version lasts
approximately 1 year. After the first year, LTS Vault versions move from
standard maintenance to extended maintenance for approximately one additional
year.

LTS version | GA        | Extended maintenance start | Extended maintenance end
----------- | --------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------
1.16.x      |  APR 2024 | MAR 2025                   | APR 2026
1.19.x      |  MAR 2025 | APR 2026                   | APR 2027

Extended maintenance includes patches for bugs that may cause outages and
critical vulnerabilities and exposures (CVEs).

Refer to the
[IBM HashiCorp Self-Managed Product Support Lifecycle Addendum](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/7258053)
support article or the
[HashiCorp Support FAQ](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/7267028)
for more details, including maintenance dates for non-LTS 1.x releases.

If you use 1.19 LTS, plan migration before the published April 30, 2027 end of
maintenance. Review the [upgrade guide](/vault/docs/upgrade) and
[important changes](/vault/docs/updates/important-changes) for your target
version, including any required intermediate upgrades.

## Release cadence FAQ

### Is this four minor releases plus one major every year?

No. Vault plans four feature release windows in total: an annual major in May
and minor releases in February, August, and November. Patch releases are a
separate monthly target.

### Why does the final minor receive patches for longer?

Intermediate minors are superseded by newer minors in the same major, which
become the destination for subsequent fixes. The final minor has no later
minor in that major to replace it. It therefore continues receiving eligible
fixes under the major's remaining lifecycle after feature development moves
to the next major.

The timeline illustrates that pattern. Its patch counts and endpoints do not
promise a fixed number of patches or establish support deadlines.

### Does the final minor start a new support period?

No. The support lifecycle begins with the major release. Minor and patch
releases do not restart it. The final minor has no new LTS designation.
Support Cycle-2 coverage varies by phase; Sustained Support does not include
new bug or security fixes.

### Where can I find end-of-support dates for Vault 2.x?

Use the [IBM Software Support Lifecycle](https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/lifecycle/)
for the authoritative Base, Extended, and Sustained Support dates. Search for
HashiCorp Vault and select the applicable Vault Self-Managed 2.x lifecycle
record. Do not infer an end-of-support date from a minor release date.

### Do I need to upgrade to every minor release?

While your major is receiving new minors, you must move to its latest minor
to receive subsequent fixes. Once you are on its final minor, you can remain
on that minor while it remains eligible for fixes, keeping its patches
current. Features introduced in a newer major require upgrading to a release
that contains them.

### Can I remain on an older major when a new major ships?

Yes, while the older major remains eligible for fixes and you run its final
minor with current patches. A new major does not immediately end fix coverage
for the previous major. Features introduced in the new major require upgrading
to a release that contains them.

### What happens when a minor stops receiving fixes?

Subsequent fixes are delivered on the newer minor within that major. The end
of new fixes for a minor is different from the end of technical support. You
may still have access to Support under your terms, but resolving an issue may
require upgrading to a release that contains the fix.

### Can I plan one feature upgrade each year?

The final minor can support a longer interval between feature upgrades, but
your plan must account for its availability and remaining fix coverage.
Do not wait for a future release if doing so creates a coverage gap. You
may need an interim upgrade, and you should continue applying eligible
patches between feature upgrades. Follow the
[upgrade guide](/vault/docs/upgrade)
for supported upgrade paths and any required intermediate versions.

### Can I upgrade directly to my chosen release?

The release policy does not define supported upgrade paths. Check the source
and target versions in the [upgrade guide](/vault/docs/upgrade), including
any required intermediate versions. Review your deployment topology and test
the upgrade before changing production environments.

### Does a monthly patch target guarantee a patch every month?

No. Monthly patches are a planning target, not a guarantee of a release for
every eligible minor each month. Use release notes to confirm available
fixes and applicable security advisories or Support guidance for a specific
issue.
